manifest.name: sdlc-harness
manifest.description: A DeepSeek Harness bundle that runs an engineering practice against a locally served model

bundle.text:
# The sdlc-harness bundle patch: this harness's persona over the dsh-base layer.
#
# A patch replaces the targeted row's whole `config`, so this row restates every
# key it relies on. Compose this bundle after the surface bundle, which sets its
# own persona on this row, and note that the browser surface reaches the persona
# below only through the preset `sdlc-harness-install` generates.

- id: system-prompt
  config:
    # The substrate's own identity section renders below the persona's order.
    includeHarnessIdentity: true
    includeRuntimeContext: true
    # `toolOrder` stays omitted: omission means lexicographic order, while an
    # explicit list must carry the `<unlisted-tools>` rest entry.
    persona: |
      You are the sdlc-harness agent: this substrate composed into a coding agent
      that runs a specific engineering practice, on the {{model}} model, in
      {{cwd}}. That practice's skills and rules, once installed, are the process
      you follow rather than one you invent per session.

      ## Voice

      - Lead with the answer or the verdict. No preamble, no restating the question.
      - Prefer many short lines to few wide ones, and break at clause boundaries.
      - Recommend rather than survey: name your pick first, then one line per
        alternative with its trade-off.
      - Say a risk plainly. A flaw softened into a hedge is a flaw you failed to report.
      - Never paste raw tool output back. Summarise to the conclusion, and quote only
        the one or two lines that carry it.
      - No em dashes. Use commas, colons, parentheses, or two sentences.
      - Call a vertical slice of work a ticket.

      ## Tools

      Your schema list is authoritative, and it is not Claude Code's. The practice's
      rules were written for that other harness, so where a rule names a tool you do
      not have, do the equivalent with the tools you do have and say that you did.
      Here, files are `read`, `write` and `edit`, searches are `glob` and `grep`,
      commands are `bash`, a skill runs through `skill`, and a question for the human
      goes through `ask_user_question`.

readme.text:
A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) bundle that
runs one engineering practice, its skills and its rules, against a model you
serve yourself. It is a bundle, not a fork: the substrate is pinned and never
modified, and this repo adds one patch layer that supplies a persona plus one
command that installs the practice's skills from their upstreams at pinned
releases.

The practice is a fixed build flow. Every step is a skill, invoked by its bare
name:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph spec ["Spec"]
    direction LR
    A["/grill-with-docs"] --> B["/to-spec"] --> C["/to-tickets"]

Six steps, in order. No prior Claude Code experience is assumed.

**1. Serve a model.** Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint whose chat template
advertises tool support. The substrate always sends the native `tools` field and
has no text-parsing fallback, so a model without declared tools cannot run here.

**2. Install the substrate and pnpm.** Node 22 or newer; `pnpm` is required
because `dsh plugin` shells out to it.

```bash
npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.0-rc.7 pnpm
```

The version is pinned on purpose: this bundle is verified against rc.7, and the
installer warns when it finds any other release.

**3. Clone this repo and add it to the browser profile.**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/brunodantas/sdlc-harness.git ~/sdlc-harness
```

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add file:$HOME/sdlc-harness
```

Use the `web` profile (created on first use) rather than building your own: it
already composes the browser surface, which is not installable on its own.

**4. Install the practice.**

```bash
node ~/sdlc-harness/bin/install.js
```

This fetches every skill at its pinned release into `~/.dsh/skills`, writes the
practice's rules to `~/.dsh/AGENTS.md` with their on-demand reference beside
them as `~/.dsh/practice-reference.md`, records what it resolved in
`~/.dsh/skills.lock.json`, and generates an agent preset named `SDLC Harness`.

**5. Boot.** A key is required even for a local server, and any non-empty string
satisfies it.

```bash
DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=local-none DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080/v1 dsh --profile web --port 7777
```

**6. Select the preset.** Open the printed URL and, in the session's mode menu,
choose **SDLC Harness** in place of Standard mode. This does not persist: a
session started without it runs the substrate's own persona and rules, and looks
identical until the agent's behaviour tells you otherwise.

Then invoke a skill by its bare name, for example `/to-cases path/to/spec.md`,
and send it with the send button (Enter does not send while the skill
autocomplete is open).

Forty skills, flattened into one unnamespaced root:

- **brunodantas/skills** at `v0.2.0` (`cc6da61`): `build-pr`, `harden-tests`,
  `ilities`, `to-cases`, `to-tests`
- **mattpocock/skills** at `v1.2.3` (`6acc160`): 35 skills; the full roster is
  in [skills.manifest.json](skills.manifest.json)

Both sources are MIT licensed and installed unmodified. Their licences travel
with the skills and apply to your copies; this repo's own MIT licence covers
only the bundle.

The biggest gap is judgment, not structure. The structure is all here: skills
load, rules are read, the flow runs in the order the practice prescribes. But in
the acceptance run, a locally served 24B ran the whole chain to completion and
froze a test file that contained no assertions. Read
[docs/worked-example.md](docs/worked-example.md) before trusting anything this
harness produces unattended.

The rest, including everything else the acceptance run found, lives in
[docs/dsh-parity-delta.md](docs/dsh-parity-delta.md). The headlines:

- **Skill tool restrictions do nothing.** The frontmatter parser silently drops
  `allowed-tools`, so every skill runs with the full tool set.
- **The hook bridge is not composed.** No `PostToolUse` or similar automation
  runs here.
- **Permission behaviour is the profile's defaults.** No equivalent of
  `acceptEdits`, and plan mode is advisory rather than enforced.
